origin.description: Extract the first word in each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

origin.details: Equivalent to stri_extract_first_boundaries with type word and skip_word_none TRUE. No word, an empty string, or a missing string is NA.
origin.value: A character vector. NA marks no word.
origin.example:
x <- stri_extract_first_words("hello world")
cat(paste0('stri_extract_first_words("hello world") returns ', x, '.\n'))

translation.description: Extract the first word in each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: None or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

translation.details: Calls stri_extract_first_boundaries with type word and skip_word_none true. No word, an empty string, or a missing string is NA.
translation.value: A list of strings. NA marks no word.
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_extract_first_words
x = stri_extract_first_words("hello world")
print(f'stri_extract_first_words("hello world") returns {x[0]}.')
